I got really terrible irritation and skin barrier damage from using this product. Not purging, no breakouts. This wasn't my first experience with a beginner retinol serum, and I used it carefully, using the "blanket" methods to sandwich 1/2 to 1 pump between layers of moisturizer (stuff I've used for years, no fragrance, minimal ingredient list, never had a reaction to it before). I used it 3 nights in a row, and slowly developed very painful, red, hot, dry, rough, stinging skin the next morning/day. I should have stopped it after night 2, b/c I my cheeks felt warm the day after night 2, but I didn't think it was a negative reaction. After my skin barrier was completely compromised by this product, on day 4, microscopic bumps appeared over every pore on my face filled with a creamy substance like pus. My whole face hurt so I probed just 1 and then left the rest alone. It took me 3 weeks to restore my damaged skin barrier, and another 2 months to get it back to healthy enough to handle other retinol products. It was the most pain I've been in from a reaction to a skincare product. I couldn't use any exfoliators of any kind for over a month. I've only had reactions of this kind once or twice before and this was by far the worst, and took the longest to heal. If you have sensitive skin, I wouldn't even patch test on your neck. Start with the back of your hand for 3-4 days in a row, then patch test for a couple nights under your ear. Be very careful.

Some may think that such spots are aging spots, but my grandmother took good care of her skin back in the day, and she didn't expose herself to the sun as much. And her dermatologist confirmed that certain dark spots on her face are due to her condition. I recommended her this serum and although she does feel her skin less textured (super smooth) and more hydrated, the serum did not help her so much with her dark spots. We didn't expect for them to go away, but we expected at least some improvement. But overall, it's an okay product!!
